Subject: Kindred Health — resilience & provider comparison (post-demo recap)

Alex — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and a proposed next-steps list so we stay aligned on what to validate in the upcoming evaluation window. I kept this focused on reliability, failover behavior, and rate-limit/error-budget impacts since that’s what Maria flagged as critical.

Key takeaways from today's session
- Redwood differentiators vs hyperscaler-managed endpoints: predictable tail latency (continuous batching + KV cache warm-starts), configurable fallback policies (model-tier routing + region failover), and token-level cost breakdown tied to per-route throttles.
- Hyperscalers typically rely on multi-tenant endpoints with opaque autoscaling and hard rate limits per API key; our Dedicated option gives reserved throughput and explicit failover to a cheaper model variant when capacity is constrained.

Proposed validation matrix (attached: kindred-resiliency-matrix.xlsx)
1) Failover dry-run (owner: Marissa) — simulate a GPU pool outage and verify: (a) automatic routing to standby region, (b) model-variant fallback within configured latency SLO, (c) no dropped requests beyond the configured error-budget policy.
2) Rate-limit burst profile (owner: Ben) — ramp to 5x baseline QPS for 10 minutes to test throttling behavior and backpressure propagation to clients; measure 95/99/999 latencies and HTTP 429 characteristics.
3) Error-budget exhaustion scenario (owner: Rishi) — construct sustained tail-latency degradation (e.g., slow kernels) and confirm: alerting triggers, graceful degradation (lower-cost model variant), and how token billing is reported during partial failures.
4) KV cache warm-up and prefix-caching check (owner: Marissa) — validate cold-start vs steady-state token performance and impact on end-to-end latency for short/long generations.

Logistics & asks
- Can you confirm Maria (security) should be on the failover dry-run invite? I added Maria's email below.
- Proposed times: next week Tue/Wed morning PT — let me know which works for your ops team.
- I attached a one-pager (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-summary.pdf) that maps the tests to decision criteria you mentioned (uptime SLA, throttling characteristics, and operational visibility).

Next steps
- If this looks good, I’ll share an invite for the dry-run and rate-limit test slots and create a shared doc with test scripts and expected metrics.

Thanks —

Thanks Rishi — quick replies inline and a couple of asks from our side.

> Proposed validation matrix (attached...)

This matches what we discussed. A few clarifications we need before scheduling:
- For the failover dry-run, what happens to in-flight requests during the GPU pool outage? Do you buffer, retry, or return 503s? We need a clear behavior to plan client-side retries.
- On the rate-limit burst profile, can you simulate per-API-key throttling + global account throttling? We have both client-level and account-level protections and want to understand how Redwood’s throttles map to our usage patterns.
- Error-budget exhaustion: what billing behavior should we expect when requests are automatically routed to a lower-cost model variant? Will token billing reflect original model attempts or final served model?

Maria (cc) — can you confirm you want to observe the dry-run, and do you have any pre-flight requirements (IP allowlist, audit logging, or specific evidence artifacts)?

Schedule-wise, Tue morning PT works for ops (we prefer 9–11am). Please send calendar invites with test rooms and call-in info.

Appreciate the matrix and the one-pager — they help a lot.

—Alex

Looping back with a compact test plan and owner commitments after Alex's questions. I'll own the rate-limit burst run; Marissa will run the failover & KV cache checks; Rishi will own the error-budget billing validation and post-test billing reconciliation.

Short plan (we'll publish scripts in the shared Drive link):
- Tuesday 09:00 PT — Failover dry-run (Marissa, owner)
  - Prep checklist: IP allowlist for Redwood test agents, SSH jump host for on-call, and enable verbose request tracing (x-request-id header).
- Tuesday 10:30 PT — Rate-limit burst (Ben, owner)
  - Steps: Gradual ramp to 5x over 60s, hold 10 min, then cool down. Collect 429 distribution, and record when throttles kick per API key vs global.
- Tuesday 11:30 PT — Error-budget exhaustion simulation (Rishi, owner)
  - Inject latency on a staging model variant to drive 99th percentile above target, confirm alerting, ensure fallback policy triggers, and validate billing tokens in usage logs.

Deliverables post-run (within 24 hours):
- Test artifact bundle (logs + summary CSV).
- Short decision memo: pass / fail + recommended next provider posture (hosted vs Dedicated).

Rishi — I'll send calendar invites and add Maria to the failover slot. Marissa/Soojin, please confirm you have access to the Drive folder and the attached spreadsheet.
